title: Feature Entry v1
description: A human-approved BOUNDARY RULE for a feature, plus a human description of what the feature is. Membership is never stored: it is recomputed from the rule against the current index, so adding an artifact to the package cannot drift an approved feature. What a reviewer approves is the rule and the prose.

kind.description: Discriminates a Feature Entry from an artifact entry for any reader that meets both.

slug.description: Identity is `Feature:<slug>` — two segments. Three would satisfy work_record.entry_relative_path's unpack and resolve to a path under ARTIFACTS_ROOT that does not exist, failing silently instead of loudly.

boundary.description: The rule, not its result. Measured on a 20-object package: depth 1 from one anchor reaches 3 objects, depth 2 reaches 13, depth 4 saturates at 17 — because each hop expands BOTH along the object's own lookups and along every field that points AT it. Depth alone therefore cannot express a feature; anchors, hubs and explicit overrides are what make the boundary a decision rather than a radius.

anchors.description: Objects the feature is built around.

hubs.description: Objects kept as an edge target but never expanded through. Without them a shared object (User, Account, a resource table) drags the whole model in at the next hop.

include.description: Identities a human declares members regardless of what the traversal finds.

exclude.description: Identities a human declares non-members regardless of what the traversal finds.

membershipAssuranceFloor.description: Weakest edge assurance allowed to carry membership. Measured: 23 of 29 Apex members of one boundary joined only through heuristic edges — a class that merely mentions the object name. A floor of source-exact keeps those out of the member list; they are still reported, counted and labelled.

approval.description: Mirrors the ledger, which is authoritative. No membership list appears here or in the ledger: a permanent human-attributed approval record must not carry cross-artifact identities the reviewer was explicitly told they were not approving, derived from a cache that is never authority.
